hint: Watch for “the” versus “a” in the English.

corpus.en: An archer does not follow elves.
The elf does not guard an archer.
The queen does not follow an eagle.
Wolves do not guard the queens.
The elves do not follow the archers.

accepted: an elf does not follow the queen
an elf did not follow the queen
an elf is not following the queen
toEnglish.explanation: S O V order. tetu = elf; natuya-mu-bo = queen-DEF-ACC; re = NEG; agi = follow.

accepted: the elves do not guard archers
the elves did not guard archers
the elves are not guarding archers
toEnglish.explanation: S O V order. tetu-ko-mu = elf-PL-DEF; tiranle-ko-bo = archer-PL-ACC; re = NEG; binte-ne = guard-3PL.

toLang.prompt: The queen does not follow archers.
toLang.explanation: S O V order. natuya-mu = queen-DEF; tiranle-ko-bo = archer-PL-ACC; re = NEG; agi = follow.

toLang.prompt: The eagle does not follow the wolf.
toLang.explanation: S O V order. tuke-mu = eagle-DEF; manto-mu-bo = wolf-DEF-ACC; re = NEG; agi = follow.
S V order. manto-mu = wolf-DEF; re = NEG; tonka = sleep.

grammar: Word order: subject, object, verb. With one participant: subject, verb.
Definite (“the”). A noun without it means “a” (or plain plural).
On the verb when the subject is plural.
Negation: a separate word before the verb.
explain.notes: Checked against 471 alternative analyses; the sentences rule out 464, including: -bo appears when: object & human; -ne appears when: plural lone-subject/object; re appears when: negative & two-participant clause.
